guideTitle: 6 Best Hose Reel Carts With Baskets in 2026
metaTitle: 6 Best Hose Reel Carts With Baskets (2026)
metaDescription: Six hose reel carts with built-in storage baskets compared on hose capacity, wheel design, steel gauge and handle comfort for tools you can grab fast.
introParagraphs: A storage basket sounds like a small extra, but it changes how a hose cart feels in use. Spray nozzles, gloves, connectors and sprinkler heads stay on the cart instead of in a pocket or on the grass. The basket is only useful if it is sturdy, sized for real tools, and does not make the cart harder to push or store.

This lineup covers six carts whose listings name a basket: the VINGLI rated for 300 feet, the Liberty Garden 13-gauge steel cart at 250 feet, the AugFir with a removable basket and 8 inch solid wheels, the Backyard Expressions with a wire basket and hammertone finish, the WERMAH with 10 inch airless tires and brass fittings, and a VEVOR 300 foot steel cart. We left out duplicate VINGLI color listings and the Poakkus, which is covered in our budget guides.

We evaluated each one based on product specs and buyer feedback, concentrating on hose capacity, basket design, wheels, fittings and handle comfort. Capacity ratings assume a standard hose, and a thicker hose reduces real length.

products.name: VINGLI 300 ft 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart With Basket

specList.label: Frame
specList.value: Water and rust resistant coated steel

products.description:
The VINGLI is the most balanced cart in this group. It holds 300 feet of 5/8 inch hose or 400 feet of 1/2 inch hose on a four-wheel frame of water and rust resistant coated steel, and it includes a storage basket. A non-slip crank grip and foam padded handle are the comfort features the listing highlights.

The listing calls the design compact and lightweight, which is unusual for a cart with this much reach and makes shed storage easier. The tradeoff is that it publishes few details on wheel size, steel gauge, or fitting material, so durability is judged on the coating claim alone. A 300 foot rating is also more than most yards need, and a full drum is still heavy to push over soft ground. The simple installation steps, with a replacement promise for missing parts, suit buyers who want a straightforward setup.

For ownership, plan a short assembly session and a spot where the four-wheel stance can sit level. The padded handle helps with long winding sessions, and the basket takes nozzles and gloves. Compared with the Liberty Garden at 250 feet, it adds 50 feet of 5/8 inch reach and padded grips. Compared with the WERMAH at 300 feet, it matches the length but does not list brass fittings or large airless tires.
products.bestFor: Larger yards that want long reach, a basket, and padded grips in a compact frame.

Coated steel resists water and rust

cons: Wheel size and fittings not detailed

products.name: Liberty Garden 250 ft 4-Wheel Steel Hose Reel Cart
products.description:
The Liberty Garden is the only cart in this group that states a steel gauge. Its frame is heavy 13-gauge steel that the listing says can withstand harsh outdoor elements and regular use throughout the year. It holds up to 250 feet of 5/8 inch hose on four wheels and includes a basket.

A crank handle winds the hose back in after you pull it off the reel, so the system is simple and mechanical. The tradeoff is weight, because 13-gauge steel adds mass that you feel when pushing a full drum across soft turf. The listing requires assembly and gives the dimensions as 24.5 by 29 by 35 inches, so measure the shed doorway before buying. It states no wheel size, no padded grip, and no fitting material, which leaves comfort and leak control as unknowns.

For ownership, expect a hands-on build and a cart that holds its shape for years if the finish stays intact. Touch up chipped coating before rust spreads. Compared with the VINGLI at 300 feet, it holds 50 feet less and lacks documented padded grips, but it is the only one that names a steel gauge. Compared with the AugFir at 250 feet, it matches the capacity in a heavier steel frame rather than aluminum alloy.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prioritize a rigid steel frame and a straightforward crank.
cons: Wheel and fitting details not listed

products.name: AugFir 250 ft Hose Reel Cart With Removable Basket
products.description:
The AugFir is built around its detachable basket. You can lift the basket off to carry nozzles, gloves, and compact pruning tools to a bed, then clip it back on when you wind up. The frame is forged from aluminum alloy with a heavy-duty metal reel, and it holds 250 feet of 5/8 inch hose.

Eight inch solid wheels and a low center of gravity are meant to avoid tipping on grass, mud, and uneven ground. An angled connector reduces kinking at the source, and a 3.9 foot water supply hose is included. The tradeoff is that solid wheels ride harder than air-filled tires, and the listing says nothing about weight limits or handle padding. Aluminum alloy resists rust but is not as rigid as thick steel under impact.

For ownership, the removable basket means you can leave the cart parked and still take tools where you are working. Compared with the Liberty Garden, it matches the 250 foot capacity and is lighter to move because of the aluminum frame. Compared with the VINGLI at 300 feet, it holds 50 feet less but adds a detachable basket and a stated wheel size. Compared with the Backyard Expressions, it states capacity and wheel size where that listing does not.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who carry tools to different beds while the cart stays parked.
pros: 8 inch solid wheels, low center of gravity
cons: Solid wheels ride harder than air tires
Not as rigid as thick steel

products.name: WERMAH 300 ft Hose Reel Cart With Brass Fittings
products.description:
The WERMAH puts its effort into the connection. A pre-installed one-piece brass connector with precision seals is meant to stop leaks, and an angled brass connector keeps the hose from kinking at the reel. It holds 300 feet of 5/8 inch hose, and a 6.5 foot leader hose is included.

The frame, T piece, and handle carry a heavy powder coat, and the listing adds stainless steel screws and rust-proof wheel hubs. Ten inch non-slip airless tires on a wide base give the stability the listing promises, and a foam padded crank grip eases winding even for children and older users. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no weight and no hose-guide details. It is also a full 300 foot cart, so it takes real storage space.

For ownership, it comes with a manual and tools, and the T piece extension bar stops the hose from turning on its own. Compared with the VINGLI at 300 feet, it is the pick if leaks and kinks are your main fear because it lists brass and an angled connector. Compared with the AugFir at 8 inch solid wheels, its 10 inch airless tires roll over more uneven ground. Compared with the Liberty Garden at 250 feet, it adds 50 feet and the leader hose.
products.bestFor: Anyone tired of dripping connections and kinked hoses.
pros: One-piece brass connector with precision seals
10 inch airless tires never go flat
cons: Weight and hose-guide details not listed
Airless tires ride firmer than air-filled

products.name: Backyard Expressions 4-Wheel Hose Reel Cart With Basket
products.description:
The Backyard Expressions cart leans on a wide four-wheel design that the listing says keeps it steady while you pull and rewind hose. A rust-resistant hammertone gray finish is meant to last season after season, and brass connectors resist rust and wear. A built-in wire basket holds sprayers, nozzles, gloves, and fittings.

The large reel and easy-turn hand crank keep the hose neat and off the ground. The tradeoff is the missing numbers: the listing states no hose capacity, steel gauge, wheel size, or weight. You will need to check the product page to confirm that the reel suits the length of hose you already own. Wire baskets drain water well but can let small connectors slip through.

For ownership, the finish should hide scuffs better than a glossy coat, and brass at the connection point is the right place to spend. Compared with the AugFir, it lacks the removable basket and the stated capacity, but the wire basket is fixed and rattle-free. Compared with the WERMAH at 300 feet, it lists brass connectors too but gives no capacity figure. It suits buyers who care about looks and a stable base more than a spec sheet.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a stable four-wheel cart with a built-in wire basket and a finish that hides scuffs.
cons: Wheel size and steel gauge not listed
Small parts can slip through the wire basket

products.name: VEVOR 300 ft Hose Reel Cart With Storage Basket
products.description:
The VEVOR holds up to 300 feet of 5/8 inch hose, with the hose not included. The structure is powder-coated steel with a weather-resistant coating and brass fittings that the listing says resist rust and leakage. A storage basket is named in the title, and a non-slip handle makes winding easier.

The listing promises a low center of gravity that helps prevent tipping. One detail needs a check before you buy: the title advertises four wheels, but the feature text describes two solid PVC wheels, so confirm the wheel setup on the product page. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no wheel diameter, weight, or steel gauge. It suits residential gardens, vehicle washing, and general cleaning according to the maker.

For ownership, assembly is the main chore, and the basket carries a nozzle and gloves. Compared with the WERMAH at 300 feet, it lists brass fittings but not an angled connector or a leader hose. Compared with the VINGLI at 300 feet, it adds named brass fittings and a stated steel finish but no padded grip. Compared with the Liberty Garden at 250 feet, it offers 50 feet more reach and a brass connection point.
products.bestFor: Large yards that want brass fittings and a steel frame without paying for extras.
pros: Brass fittings resist rust and leaks
cons: Wheel count unclear between title and text
Wheel size and weight not listed

buyingCriteria.explanation: A basket should hold real tools without rattling them out, and it should not make the cart top-heavy. The AugFir has a detachable basket, the Backyard Expressions has a built-in wire basket, and the WERMAH, VINGLI, Liberty Garden, and VEVOR include baskets with fewer details. Removable baskets are useful for carrying tools to a bed, while wire baskets drain water but let small connectors slip through. Keep heavy items low in the basket and sharp tools sheathed.

Ratings assume a standard hose, and a thicker hose takes more drum space so real length drops. The VINGLI and WERMAH rate 300 feet of 5/8 inch hose, the VEVOR rates 300 feet, and the Liberty Garden and AugFir rate 250. The VINGLI also rates 400 feet of 1/2 inch hose. Choose a rating at least 10 percent above your longest hose, because overfilling makes the crank stiff and winds the hose unevenly.

A thicker frame resists flex and rattling under a full 250 or 300 feet of water-filled hose. The Liberty Garden states heavy 13-gauge steel, the AugFir uses forged aluminum alloy, and the others name coated or powder-coated steel without a gauge. Check the finish for chips each season, because that is where rust starts. A lighter aluminum frame will push easier, but a thick steel frame will tolerate impacts better.

Wheels decide how the cart rolls and whether it tips. The AugFir uses 8 inch solid wheels with a low center of gravity, the WERMAH uses 10 inch non-slip airless tires on a wide base, and the Backyard Expressions has a wide four-wheel stance. Solid and airless wheels never go flat but ride harder over bumps. Larger wheels roll over roots and soft turf with less effort, so favor 10 inches if your lawn is uneven.

The connection point is where hose reels start dripping and kinking. The WERMAH lists a one-piece brass connector with an angled design and a 6.5 foot leader hose, the AugFir lists an angled connector, and the VEVOR and Backyard Expressions list brass. An angled connector lets the hose leave the reel without a hard bend. If you leave the hose pressurized, choose brass and replace the washer every spring.

You turn the crank every time you wind, so grip comfort matters for wrists. The VINGLI has a foam padded handle with a non-slip crank grip, and the WERMAH adds a foam-padded crank grip that the listing says even children and older users can handle. A heavy cart is harder to push and store, so the Liberty Garden's 13-gauge frame trades weight for rigidity. Measure your shed door against the Liberty Garden's 24.5 by 29 by 35 inches before buying.

howWeEvaluated.title: Basket usefulness
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared basket design, from the AugFir's detachable basket to the Backyard Expressions' fixed wire basket. We looked at whether the listing says what the basket holds and whether it is removable. Listings that only named a basket in the title were rated cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hose capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We used stated ratings, with the VINGLI, WERMAH, and VEVOR at 300 feet and the Liberty Garden and AugFir at 250 feet. The Backyard Expressions states no capacity, so it was marked down for transparency. All figures assume a standard 5/8 inch hose.

howWeEvaluated.title: Frame and fittings
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared steel, aluminum alloy, and powder-coated finishes, and noted that the Liberty Garden names 13-gauge steel while the AugFir uses aluminum alloy. Brass fittings on the WERMAH, VEVOR, and Backyard Expressions counted as a reliability point. We did not run durability tests.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wheels and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: Wheel size and type were weighed, from the AugFir's 8 inch solid wheels to the WERMAH's 10 inch airless tires. The VEVOR's conflicting wheel description was treated as an open question. Scores reflect stated design and buyer feedback, not measured trials.

howWeEvaluated.title: Comfort and value
howWeEvaluated.description: Handle padding, crank grips, and ease of assembly were weighed. The VINGLI leads on padded grips and reach, the WERMAH on leak control and included leader hose, and the Liberty Garden on named steel gauge. We compared what each listing includes in the box.

faq.q: Why six picks and not more?
faq.a: Several listings are near duplicates, including VINGLI color variants and the VEVOR and Poakkus carts we cover elsewhere. We kept six distinct models with a named basket. Listings that merely repeated an existing cart were left out.

faq.q: What can I put in the basket?
faq.a: Spray nozzles, gloves, connectors, and sprinkler heads fit best. The AugFir also lists compact pruning tools, and the Backyard Expressions lists sprayers and fittings. Keep sharp tools sheathed and heavy items low.

faq.q: How much hose will it hold?
faq.a: The VINGLI, WERMAH, and VEVOR hold 300 feet of 5/8 inch hose, and the Liberty Garden and AugFir hold 250 feet. The VINGLI also holds 400 feet of 1/2 inch hose. Thicker hose lowers capacity, and the Backyard Expressions does not state a figure.

faq.q: Are solid or airless wheels better than air-filled tires?
faq.a: They never go flat and need no pressure checks, but they ride harder over bumps. The AugFir uses 8 inch solid wheels and the WERMAH uses 10 inch airless tires. Both suit lawns, gravel, and light slopes.

faq.q: Will a basket make the cart tip?
faq.a: A heavy basket can raise the center of gravity and make the cart tip when you pull the hose at an angle. The AugFir lists a low center of gravity and the WERMAH a wide base. Keep heavy items low and pull in a straight line.

Wind evenly and do not overfill beyond the rated length. The AugFir and WERMAH list angled connectors, which let the hose leave the reel without a hard bend. A short leader hose, like the 6.5 foot one included with the WERMAH, also relieves stress at the reel.

faq.q: Is a 300 foot cart too big for a small yard?
faq.a: Usually yes, because a full drum is heavy and the frame takes shed space. A 250 foot cart such as the Liberty Garden or AugFir is easier to store. Buy for the longest run you truly need plus a small margin.
